text: We were never supposed to eat three meals a day. It's a lie. Here's why. For most of human history, people ate once a day. The Romans thought breakfast was for the week. Greek philosophers fasted to think clearly. Monks like me have eaten one meal a day for over 2,000 years. Then factories were built. Workers needed to stay awake for 12-hour shifts. So they invented a schedule. Breakfast, lunch, dinner. Three meals to keep the machines running. You inherited that schedule. Not your hunger. Not your biology. A factory clock. Every time you eat, your insulin spikes. Your body stops repairing itself. Your gut never rests. That's why you feel tired at 3 p.m. That's why you're hungry an hour after lunch. You're not weak. You were trained. Try this for seven days. Eat one meal when the sun is high. Water the rest of the day. Watch what happens to your mind. The full path is in my book, The Way Back to Stillness. Link in my profile.
